_help.about: Torchfire 1, the ambient first-person dungeon crawler. The open world is Torchfire 2 and stays in the code, switched off (§ET.2). First guesses by Claude (chat), 6 Oct; the designer owns them. Wired 6 Oct (Claude Code, the first slice, §ET.11): data/game.json picks the game; scenes/crawler.tscn builds the hearth room and the tomb (scripts/crawler/).
_help.opening: §ET.3. You wake underground in a ruin's central room by a lit hearth. exits_min / exits_max: corridors leaving it, each generated from the seed. bundle: unlit torches by the hearth (torch.json bundle, §AW). rescuer: the figure who found you and brought you here (§DE), at the hearth. teach: wordless, no tooltips. first_theme: the theme of the first ruin (a key of themes). Built: exits_min..exits_max corridors from the seed; the bundle by the hearth (torch.json bundle.count_at_camp torches), taken one at a time with the interact button; the rescuer standing at the hearth as a baked sprite (sprites, rescuer); since §FH (7 Oct) sitting at the hearth on a low stone, live in 3D (folk_3d, rescuer).
_help.persistence: Confirmed by Mike 7 Oct (§FK.2; was §ET.10 call 3, Claude's reading): a new game rolls one seed (seed: one_per_new_game) and every world and dungeon comes from it; the layout is new each new game and the same within a game, kept for good. relit_stays_lit, gates_keep_state: restored stays restored. dungeon_seeds: from_game_seed, each dungeon's seed drawn from the game's, so the same game always makes the same next dungeon (replaces exit.stand_in's new seed). save: the seed and what changed (lights relit, gates, ruins restored, worlds found) in a save. continue: last_world, Continue opens your world where you left it, New game rolls a new seed (Claude's first guess; one world or slots open, §FK.5 call 3). Built 9 Oct (Claude Code, queue 63; CrawlerSave, CrawlerMain, the boot scene's BootMenu): seed: a new game rolls one (1-999999). dungeon_seeds: the first dungeon (place 0: §FJ.1's pick once wired, the tomb until then) is built from the game's own seed, so SEED= pins the tombs the checks always knew; each place after it (the next dungeon each way out leads to, 1, 2, ...) from a seed drawn from the game's seed and the place, so exit.stand_in now takes the game's next dungeon, the same every time for that game. save: crawler_save (was world_save, Claude's first guess; changed by Claude Code, 9 Oct): the crawler keeps its own save beside the open world's, user://crawler/<game seed>.json, with user://crawler/last.json naming the last game (WorldSave keeps user://worlds and its own last for Torchfire 2, so the two games never open each other's worlds). It holds the game's seed, the place you are in, and per dungeon its seed, theme, a fingerprint of its holders and the holders you relit (by index in the layout's order; a dungeon whose layout no longer matches its fingerprint starts cold, with a warning), written whenever it changes (a new game, a holder catching, a walk out) and when the game closes. The tools never write it: under WorldSave.read_only or in any --script run it lives in memory only. relit_stays_lit: true lights them again on Continue, straight away and with no log line (false: kept, but every light starts cold). A dungeon kept with every light relit comes back cleared (§FF.2: its residents bones in their places) and its boss down its hole (§EY.2), with no log lines again. continue: last_world: with a game kept the boot shows a plain choice, Continue (the last game, in the dungeon you were in, at its hearth, its relit holders burning; log_continue is the log's line then, added) or New game (asks twice, rolls a new seed); with no game kept it opens on a new one. Anything else: no Continue, every start a new game. Settings' New world line reads New game in the crawler and does the same. SEED= in the environment pins a game, a fresh start of it at its first dungeon. gates_keep_state: waits for gates (CrawlerSave.keep holds any dungeon's named state for them); the first, §FM.6's fork (queue 68, descent.json fork), is kept as fork_open: once its seal has gone it stays gone, and Continue opens it at once, quietly (as it does with every light on floor one kept relit). Not kept yet: the torches you carry, the bundle's count and the clock (each start opens at the world's start time).
_help.themes: §ET.5. Stage themes, each a ruin of its biome. ruin_kind: the ruins.json / delves.json kind its rooms come from (open where no kind fits yet). air: still or drafty (torch.json snuff.draft). dark: how dark before you relight it. space: tight or exposed. frames: Project-sheet reference frames. Only the two Mike named are listed; §CJ's delve types and the monuments (§DN–§DZ) are the pool for more. Built: tomb only (the first slice). air still: only ordinary drafts plus airways.still strong mouths; dark pitch: crawler.json look. stone (Claude Code, 7 Oct, §EX.1): the theme's own stone colour, what masonry.json styles stone.tint "theme" means: the tomb's is #636870, the mean colour its fitted walls showed before §EX (RuinBuilder's five grey tones darkened as the walls drew them), so the walls keep their tone; the snow ruins' is a first guess (paler, colder), not built.
_help.progress: §ET.4. Relit fire-holders (delves.json fire_holders) stay lit for the game and are places to relight a torch. Items are keys, tools and knowledge only (item_kinds): no damage numbers, no rarity, no chests (§CJ.3). Built: relit_is_progress (the log counts the holders relit). item_kinds and gates are not built yet.
_help.gates: §ET.4. Puzzle gates to rediscover, never traps to punish. kinds: the ones talked through (PSO's obelisk set; a code from a found scroll; a passage that opens once relit). How each works is Claude Code's call within §ET. relight_to_open built 9 Oct (Claude Code, queue 68; RelightGate, Fork): the fork's seal (descent.json fork), a plain stone slab in a doorway that sinks into its floor when every holder on floor one is relit; it shuts the way down; the way out stays open (§EX.5), unless fork.gate_surface is set true (§FM.10 call 2, Mike's), when a second seal shuts the foot of its flight too. The obelisk set and the scroll code are not built.
_help.sprites: §ET.8. Figures and creatures are sprites baked from the shared rig (painted per §ES). around: directions around the figure (Doom's eight). rows_deg: viewing heights, the camera's elevation above the figure's eye line in degrees (negative is from below); the nearest row is drawn. anim_fps: the sprite animation's own steppy rate; the game still renders at full rate. sprite / geometry: what is and is not a sprite. candidates: small things with no engine shape yet, sprite candidates (first guess). Built for the rescuer (FigureSprite): around x rows_deg frames, each a still of the shared rig painted per §ES; anim_fps steps its idle (rescuer.idle_frames). Since §FH (7 Oct) folk are live 3D (folk_3d), so sprite's "folk" is §ET.8's word: FigureSprite waits for creatures and bosses (folk_3d.sprites_stay_for), kept, compiled and checked (crawler_check checks its frames; crawler_frames bakes a sheet), drawing nothing in the tomb yet.
_help.kit: (Claude Code, 6 Oct, §ET.11 2; first guesses, Mike tunes by playing) The tomb kit (§CJ.8, TombKit): rooms and corridors from the seed, axis-aligned stone, stairs going down. hearth_room: the central room's size (m, len x width, h ceiling). branch_rooms: rooms down each exit's branch [min, max]. corridor_m: a corridor's length [min, max]; corridor_half_m: half its width; corridor_h_m: its ceiling. stair_chance: a corridor that goes down a flight instead (stair_drop_m per flight, slope stair_slope). room_m: a room's length and width [min, max]; room_h_m: its ceiling. turn_chance: a branch turning left or right at a room instead of going straight on. kinds: the tomb's rooms and their weights (crypt: sarcophagi in rows; catacomb: bone niches along long walls; ossuary: bones heaped; collapsed: a fallen ceiling slab and rubble). The spine's last room is the heart (§CJ.3, plan: the dead laid out, the frame-9 skeleton leaning out of its mossy stone box). Since 7 Oct (Claude Code, §EX.2, queue 46): every size is whole modules of the theme's style (masonry.json styles module_m, the tomb's 2 m): room_m and corridor_m each pick a whole number of modules inside their range (6, 8 or 10 m; a flight at least its drop at stair_slope, rounded up), the hearth room's sides snap to the nearest (9 m to 10 m); the ceilings are the style's heights_m (corridor 2.6, room 3.2, hearth room 3.6 m; corridor_h_m, room_h_m and hearth_room h_m stand in for a style that names none). branch_rooms and turn_chance are the side ways' (the spine's rooms are plan.spine.rooms, and it runs straight). A crypt only in a room at least 8 m wide, so an aisle stays clear between the coffins' askew lids.
_help.holders: (Claude Code, 6 Oct, §ET.11 3; amended 7 Oct for §EX.4; delves.json fire_holders gives light_radius_m, holds_units and skip) The cold fire-holders. rooms: room_torches (§EX.4: every room past the hearth room has wall sconces; until 7 Oct each had a hearth ring from delves.json by_ruin tomb, which still serves the open world). Corridors have a wall sconce every sconce_every_m (first one sconce_first_m in; none in corridors shorter than that; none on stairs). They start cold and dark, with the ash of the last fire laid (laid: no kindling needed, the swing lights them, §CN), and once relit they stay lit (kept: they never burn down, §ET.4) and you can relight a torch at them. sconce_h_m: the sconce's flame height; sconce_scale: its flame against a campfire's. Since 7 Oct (§EX.5, queue 46): a cold holder's light is off from the start, however far down the tomb it lies (the spine is long). (7 Oct, §EX.3) A sconce now sits in a trapezoid niche cut into its wall's fitted stone, its flame in a stone cup, its light 0.32 m out in front of the niche, where the old bracket held it (masonry.json styles sconce; CrawlerFires.LIGHT_OUT_M); sconce_h_m is where the flame stands, the cup's top.
_help.look: (Claude Code, 6 Oct, §ET.11 3: full dark between the lights, §BA, §CJ.5) Underground there is no sun or sky: ambient_color / ambient_energy are the dark's own faint navy (never grey, never quite black), fog_color / fog_density its depth. The tomb is lit only by fire. fire_shadow_mode: the casting fires' shadow kind (look.json fire_shadows picks which cast): cube (six faces) here, because a torch or sconce in a corridor is always a step from a big flat wall, where the open world's cheaper dual_paraboloid warps into curved dark blots; the two nearest still cast only.
_help.airways: (Claude Code, 6 Oct, §ET.6, §ET.7; amended 7 Oct for §EZ.5; torch.json snuff.draft) The builders' airways: slots in corridor walls breathing toward open air. None of them ever puts the torch out or gutters it (§EZ.5: only deep water does). per_air: how many of each kind a tomb gets by its theme's air (still / drafty): ordinary ones lean the flame (lean_mps at the mouth, falling to nothing by reach_m) and quicken its light's flicker a little (flicker: 0-1 at the mouth, falling the same way, as §EV.3's draft flickers a vented fire; it was gutter until §EZ.5); strong ones are marked (a carved surround and a dust fan below) and blow on a cycle every_s [min, max] for gust_s, heard (a rising moan) and seen (dust streaming) snuff.draft.warn_s before; the gust reaches line_m out from the mouth, line_half_m either side of its line, and whips the torch hard away from the mouth (its smoke streams flat and its light flickers by the full flicker) while it holds; a wall between the mouth and the flame shelters it.
_help.rescuer: (Claude Code, 6 Oct, §ET.3, §ET.8; 7 Oct, §FH) The one who found you, sitting across the hearth on a low stone, facing it: the shared rig (CloakedFigure) live in 3D (folk_3d, HearthFolk), its cloak rolled from cloaks.json by the seed, beast: a zodiac head (zodiac_heads.json) or "" for the empty hood; "seed" picks one from the seed. height_m. stand_m: how far from the hearth's middle it sits (the name is from when it stood). round_deg: how far round the hearth from straight across from your mat it sits (degrees; it sits lower than the flame, so straight across the fire hid it), on whichever side keeps it and its things farther from the doors. seat_h_m: the stone's height (m), the room's own stone, in the tomb's collision; the rig sits at its own seat height (about 0.32 m at this height), and a higher or lower stone lifts or sinks it to match. breath: its idle, a slow breath, the chest's rise as a share of its height (the shoulders, the arms and the hood ride it; 0 sits still); breath_s: one breath every so many seconds. px, idle_frames: the baked sprite's frame height (pixels) and idle frames (§ET.8), not read since §FH made the rescuer live 3D. Since 9 Oct (Claude Code, §FM.6, queue 67) it reads as the shaman: the same rig, the same idle, wordless (§ED), and in its right hand one of the shared props (holds: "ladle", a long wooden ladle, the fire circle's stick with a bowl at its end; "" nothing). ladle (first guesses): handle_m (its length), below_fist_m (how much of it is under the fist), handle_r_m [at its foot, at its top], bowl_r_m, bowl_deep_m, bowl_tilt_deg (its bowl open to the sky, tipped this far toward the fire, so it reads as a scoop, not a disc), out_deg (how far it leans out to its right from upright) and fwd_deg (and toward the fire), color. Painted per §ES like the rig (the rig's own material and big texels, folk_3d.texels_per_m), casting the fire's shadow; nothing new in the rig.
_help.cauldron: (Claude Code, 9 Oct, §FM.6, queue 67; first guesses, Mike tunes by playing) The cauldron over the hearth, in every dungeon's hearth room from the first moment (HearthCauldron, built with the tomb). material: iron (§FL.1, metal allowed again; Claude Code's call among the ruin's stone, clay or iron: iron reads as a cauldron at 480 lines). hangs_from: a tripod, three poles lashed at the top, their feet on the middle of the hearth pit's kerb (inside its guard; among the old ring's stones where a style has no pit), one straight across the fire from your mat, two at the mat's sides, so none stands between you and the fire or the shaman and none of their shadows falls on you or him; the bail's arch faces your mat. empty: empty at rest; since queue 72 (§FM.7, Brew, data/brew.json) the shaman's brew stands in it only while he works a cutting you bring him, and it is served out into his ladle. pot: belly_r_m (its widest), mouth_r_m (inside its lip), h_m (bottom to rim), bottom_m (its bottom over the room's floor: the flame licks it), wall_m, lip_m (the rolled lip), sides (round), hull_top_m (the top of its collision hull, under the rim: the hull keeps out of every line from the hearth's light to the floor past the kerb, so the light field is unchanged). bail: r_m, its rod. chain: link_m (a link's length), rod_m; as many links as reach the bail. tripod: apex_m (over the floor), pole_r_m, past_apex_m (the poles' ends past the lashing), sides. firelight: the hearth's amber on it, live, from the flame under its belly: the hearth's own light hangs a hand over the pot's mouth and would light the empty pot from inside like a brazier, so that light passes the cauldron by (its cull mask leaves out the cauldron's render layer and nothing else) and the cauldron takes the fire's light from at_m over the floor, range_m, attenuation, its strength share of the hearth light's every frame and its colour the hearth light's, lighting the cauldron alone, with no shadow. colors: iron, soot (the belly toward the fire), pole, pole_soot (the poles toward the top, smoked), cord (the lashing). Nothing of the pot casts a shadow (it hangs right under the hearth's light); the poles do.
_help.plan: A thoughtful layout. module: the style's module_m (masonry.json styles, by the theme's style_by_theme); kit.room_m, kit.corridor_m and the hearth room's sides snap to whole modules. spine: one of the hearth room's ways is the main axis, the longest branch, through the heart to the exit (crawler.json exit); never a dead end. side_branches: the other ways, at most side_share of the spine's rooms each, and each ends in a room (end_in room), never a bare corridor. doors: centred on the wall they cut; facing: where a room has two doors, they face each other so you look through one to the next light. The style's plan (masonry.json styles plan) shapes the rest: gallery_and_chambers, side chambers off a main gallery; passage_and_chambers, fewer larger chambers off a long low passage. First guesses by Claude (chat), 6 Oct. Built 7 Oct (Claude Code, queue 46; TombKit): the module as kit says; the spine grown first, straight on through every room (its two doors facing: the main axis), spine.rooms rooms [min, max] (added: 4 to 5), its last the heart, at least spine.heart_min_m long (added: 8 m, room for the dead lying across it and the walk round them to the way out); the side ways at most side_share of its rooms (branch_rooms each, the share rounding down), straight on through facing doors but turning at a room by kit.turn_chance, and turning where straight on won't fit; every door centred on its wall; the spine's doors always facing, elsewhere wherever a way goes straight on. The style's own plan key is not read yet (the tomb's gallery is its spine).
_help.exit: Always a way out (Mike, 6 Oct: "at least one exit whether all the lights are activated or not"). min: exits a dungeon has at least. never_gated: no gate, puzzle or count of relit lights between the wake spot and an exit; gates (§ET.4) may close only side ways and shortcuts. place: spine_end_past_heart, the far end of the spine beyond the heart. form: stair_up, the old way in, a long flight climbing out (rise_m in all, first guess). daylight_at_top: a faint cool glow at the top (§EV.2's colours), seen from below. leads_to: §EW.3's seam to the next world, or the surface above (§EW.7 step 2). stand_in: until either is built, walking out fades (fade_s) to the next dungeon from a new seed, arriving in its hearth room, the hearth lit (§EX.9 call 3 is the real answer). check: the build fails any seed where the player's own body cannot walk from the wake spot to an exit with every holder cold and every gate shut (stairs climbable, doors wide and tall enough, nothing across a doorway). First guesses by Claude (chat), 6 Oct. Built 7 Oct (Claude Code, queue 46; TombKit._way_out, TombBuild, WayOut, CrawlerMain.walk_out): one way out per tomb (min 1), never gated (none are built; TombKit marks every spine piece and door for whoever builds them). From a door centred in the heart's far wall a flight climbs rise_m at kit.stair_slope (whole modules: 10 m for 6 m), through a door into a landing (landing_m: long and wide, added; snapped to modules) and the opening in its far wall, the threshold running on outside under the daylight to a stop. glow (added): the opening's sheet of sky (sheet_share of a vent's sky disc by day; at night it keeps sheet_night of that, on the night's darker blue, so the way out still shows faintly from below) and a soft wash falling in over the landing and the top of the flight (light_share of a shaft's daylight, reaching reach_m), in smoke.json vents.daylight's colours on the world's clock, stronger as the sun climbs, as the shafts are (Vents.sun_light_at, §FG). stand_in.log (added): the log's line as you go. Stepping into the opening is the stand-in: the game's next dungeon (since queue 63, §FK.2: its seed drawn from the game's seed and its place, persistence.dungeon_seeds, so the same walk every time for that game), and you keep what you carry, the torch lit or not as it was. check: tools/crawler_check.gd walks the player's own body (CrawlerPlayer's capsule, floor rules and step) from the wake spot out of 203 tombs. glow near_m, far_m, far_share (added by Claude Code, 7 Oct, first guesses; Mike: "the way out might not always be night; it should be relatively faint from far away but depends on time of day"): the opening's sheet of sky shows all its glow within near_m of your eye and eases down to far_share of it by far_m (WayOut.far_fade); by day and by night on the clock as before. The wash falling in is the stone's own light and doesn't fade with your distance. Moved 7 Oct (Claude Code): near_m 8 to 16 and far_m 30 to 40, so the foot of the flight (about 15 m below the opening) sees all of it: at 8 the night frame from the foot of the stairs (crawler_frames 25b) fell under its readable step (0.085 against the stone's 0.071), and §EX.5 wants the way out seen from there; from the heart and further it fades. Since 9 Oct (Claude Code, queue 71, §FM.7): leads_to is built for a dungeon with its surface (worlds.json surface: on, its theme one of over_themes; the tomb): stepping into the opening fades (surface.arrive.fade_s) to the ruin over the stair on the surface above, the dungeon kept as you left it, and the stairhead's steps lead back down to the landing, its relit holders still lit. stand_in stays for any dungeon with no surface yet (surface.on false, or a theme not over_themes).
_help.room_torches: One hearth per dungeon; every other room gets wall torches (Mike, 6 Oct: "only one main hearth room with the other rooms just having torch areas to light"). hearth_rooms: per dungeon. room_holder: sconce (in the style's own sconce, masonry.json styles sconce). small_room_max_m: a room up to this long gets small sconces, a longer one large; heart: the heart's count, heart_flank_dead of them either side of the dead. placement: facing pairs on the long walls, on the module. Corridors keep holders as built. For Torchfire 1 this replaces delves.json fire_holders.by_ruin (a hearth ring in every room); delves.json is unchanged for the open world. With §EV only the hearth gets a shaft, every sconce a flue. First guesses by Claude (chat), 6 Oct (§EX.9 call 2). Built 7 Oct (Claude Code, queue 47; TombKit, CrawlerFires): the hearth room's hearth is the only hearth and the only shaft of daylight. A room's length is its long walls' length; the long walls are its longer pair (in a square room, the pair with fewer doors). Its sconces stand in facing pairs on them, one module apart or more (the style's module_m, 2 m in the tomb), spread evenly; the heart's are heart_flank_dead on each side wall, one module apart, centred on the dead (their stone box lies across the room 1.6 m from its end wall). Built-only keys: clear_m, the least gap between a sconce's bracket and a door's edge or a corner (where a door is in the way the pairs step along the wall a quarter metre at a time, nearest first, still facing and still whole modules apart, so a door in the middle of a wall ends up flanked; failing that they take another whole-module spacing, and failing that each long wall finds its own places, the pair then not quite facing: under 1% of pairs in 400 tombs; the airways keep the same gap from the sconces); light_scale, a room sconce's light against a corridor sconce's (same flame, same reach). Measured on seeds 1, 7 and 42 (tools/crawler_check.gd: the light on each room's floor and walls, each spot counted no brighter than white): at 1.0 the dimmest small room has 0.81 of its old hearth ring's light, at 1.25 0.97, at 1.5 1.13; large rooms and the heart come out about twice as lit as with their ring. The dressing makes room: a crypt's coffin rows are set so the first sconce on a wall falls between two coffins (where that costs no coffin; one over a coffin's head is swung at from the gap beside it); a catacomb leaves out the column of bone niches a sconce hangs in; bone heaps, a collapse's slab and rubble and grave goods keep a bay clear before each sconce. pillared (Mike, 7 Oct, picking (b) of queue 48's three): a room that stands on pillars (TombBuild.on_pillars: its slabs' shorter span past its corbels over the style's max_span_m, every room 8 m or more both ways) gets this many, two facing pairs, whatever its length, because its pillars shadow a single pair's light off the floor; it may still read a little darker than its old ring, with the pillars' shadows across it (Mike: "it's also ok if there's some shadows or a bit darker than it was because it gives monsters a place to hide").
_help.firelight: One firelight: amber (Mike, 6 Oct: "always amber colored instead of the bluer spectrum"). color: every fire's light, the hearth's (look.json fire.light.color); torch.json light.color now matches it. one_hue: a torch, a planted torch, a sconce, a brazier and a hearth differ in reach and strength only. grade: firelit surfaces are left to the fire as hearth light is (look.json grade protect_*), the bright stone right at the torch included; the night grade's cyan-white pull and teal never reach them. gutter: guttering dims and reddens the coal, never cooler toward white or blue. unchanged: the dark past the fire's reach (look) and a vent's daylight column (§EV.2, sky not fire) stay blue. Built 7 Oct (Claude Code): Torch.fire_color() reads look.json fire.light.color for the torch, planted torches, sconces and hearths; guttering reddens the torch's light (Torch.gutter_color) and its coal. The cause of the pale torchlight was the torch's own old colour (#FFB347); with the amber, a torch 1 m from a wall reads the hearth's hue. Right at the stone the light blows out (each channel clips, amber through yellow to white) and the night grade's cyan-white pull and the bloom took it: pale_to_amber (0-1) puts bright pale or white pixels that aren't blue back on the fire's amber before the grade (shaders/post_grade.gdshader fire_whites): the paler the more, fully under pale_chroma[0] (chroma: brightest minus darkest channel) and not at all over pale_chroma[1], so a flame's strong tongues and deep amber stone are left alone; lift how far toward white that amber is lifted (the fire's colour mixed with white). Off in the open world.
_help.hud: reticle: the crosshair shows in first person in the crawler, the open world's (from: hud.json reticle), inside the 480-line frame (§Y); the Settings switch hud.reticle still turns it off. words: none (§ET.3 stands). warms_near_flame: an idea, not locked (§EX.9 call 4): the reticle warms when a cold holder, or a lit one for an unlit torch, is in swing reach. Built 7 Oct (Claude Code, §EX.7): reticle true puts the crosshair in the crawler's HUD (Reticle, the same code the open world's StatusHud draws it with, so the two can't drift apart), drawn over the finished frame (no grade, no dither, no bloom), on the frame's own pixel grid round its middle pixel, sized per hud.json reticle at every pixel-size preset; it hides while the log or the settings panel is open (both cover the middle of the frame). Nothing else from the open world's HUD comes with it, and no words. warms_near_flame stays false and is not built: nothing reads it yet. While you sneak (§FC.1, prompt 53, 7 Oct) it takes stealth.json sneak.reticle: the arms close into a small ring, dimmed.
_help.dark: (design §FC.4) A dark you can half see in (Mike, 6 Oct, 22:32): without a flame, the walls, floor and openings stay readable in faint navy to readable_m, and the dark is fully black by black_m. Shade stays navy, never grey. First guesses; Claude Code tunes by eye. Built 7 Oct (Claude Code, HalfDark): one weak light at your eye in readable_color, so it only ever adds navy, never warmth; no shadow, no shine. Its reach is black_m: nearly even out to about readable_m, fading to nothing at black_m. fill_energy is its strength on a wall facing you at readable_m (raise it for a brighter half-dark, lower it for a darker one; under about 1.5 the grade's navy floor swallows it and nothing shows). falloff adds dimming with distance on the way (0: even, the build; 1: brighter close, gone sooner). It is off at once while your torch is lit, and off (eased over fade_s seconds) while a lit fire, a planted torch, or a fire pot's fire or lit wick is within its own light's reach of you with a clear line to it, so the torch's reach and the lit rooms look just as before; with neither, it eases up over adjust_s seconds, your eyes adjusting.
_help.floors: (design §FF.1) A ruin can have several floors; in some you climb toward the surface, in some you go down (Mike). §EX.5's exit is at the far end. hearth_per: 'dungeon' (§EX.4) until Mike answers §FI.2 call 9. Built 9 Oct (Claude Code, queue 68, design §FM.6): the floors are data/descent.json floors (TombFloors): floor one, where you wake, and floor two below it down a stair from near the far end of the spine; hearth_per dungeon (floor two has no hearth); exit_at far_end: the way out stays past the heart at the far end of floor one, up (several and directions as given: the way up and the way down both leave floor one, the fork, descent.json fork). A ruin you climb out of from its bottom floor is not built.
_help.cleared: (design §FF.2) A floor with every light relit is cleared: its residents leave, seen going into holes and out of windows (Mike). Half-lit, they fall back into the dark pockets and counterattack anyone who comes close (residents.json rules). Built (Claude Code, 7 Oct, queue 59; Residents, Resident): until floors exist (§FF.1) a floor is the whole dungeon, so it is cleared when every holder on it is relit (when). residents_leave: then every resident leaves by its retreat_to (residents.json creatures). retreat_seen: one you can see goes in plain view, the one time they move where you can see them. Since Mike's note of 7 Oct ('creatures shouldnt "sink" into the stone'; Claude Code) every one, seen or not, hurries by the dimmest way (light_field) to its own niche or grave (or a nearer one left open), climbs in and lies down, and from then on it is bones, set dressing for good, off the roll and never waking; one too far off keeps walking there however long it takes, and nothing vanishes. The floor counts as cleared at the last light all the same (the log's line). retreat_seen_s is no longer read (it was how long one could be seen going before it was gone anyway). half_lit_pockets_bite: until then they keep to the dark and strike from it (residents.json rules). log_line: the log's one line when the floor is cleared (Claude Code's words; no creature named, §BA). The boss's release is its own (bosses.json release). Floors exist since queue 68 (Claude Code, 9 Oct, design §FM.6; descent.json floors): each floor is cleared on its own, when every holder on it is relit, its own residents leaving and the line once a floor; floor one's clearing is also what opens the fork (descent.json fork).
_help.light_field: Claude Code's first guesses on Mike's note of 7 Oct ('creatures that are actively chasing will chase near the fire but stay somewhat in the darkness if they can'; 'the snake and other physical bosses have to move thru lit room while doing their best to stay at the edges of the light'). LightField (scripts/crawler/light_field.gd) on the creatures' floor grid (TombNav): the firelight on each quarter-metre square of floor. of: which fires count: every permanent fire burning (the hearth, every relit holder, and while planted is true every planted torch), never the torch in your hand (the snake's torch_delay covers it) nor a fire pot's fire (it burns out). Each lights the squares it has a clear line to, from its light to a body's middle body_m over the square, as the renderer lights them: its light's energy times Godot's falloff, (1 - (d / range)^4)^2 / d^attenuation, d never counted under min_d_m; a square's light is the sum, and a fire's share under least is left out. Worked out again whenever a fire catches, goes out or is planted. What reads it: a chase stands only where the light is at most residents.json rules.chase_light_cap (the edge of the light); a creature crossing lit ground (cut off from the dark, out of a room relit round it, home at the last light, the snake fleeing to its lair) takes the dimmest way: each square costs 1 + dim_weight times its light over that cap, at most dim_max times, so it keeps to the edges of the light and the dark corners.
_help.restored: [NOT WIRED YET — design §FF.3] When a whole ruin is relit its people come back (Mike): a living workplace you can return to, a fire to relight from, and folk who teach a technique or give an item (§BN). You never craft.
_help.ambience: Design §FG. Atmosphere, never puzzles (Mike): glow-moss on damp stone that dims when a flame comes near and comes back after; daylight through windows and vents that follows the clock; stairs up to windows over the wilderness; beetles and scarabs that scatter from torchlight; vines that sway as you pass. glow_moss colour and numbers are first guesses (it gives off light, so it glows; never amber). Built 7 Oct (Claude Code, queue 61): glow_moss, wall_life and daylight_follows_clock. glow_moss (GlowMoss): patches on the tomb's dressed walls, height_m up from the floor, only where the stone is damp: the wet field the moss itself grows by (§EU.4: masonry.json overgrowth.wet over the theme's climate) plus airway_damp at an airway's mouth, falling to nothing by near_airway_m, at damp_min or over; never on dry stone, never within clear_of_fire_m of a fire (its soot burnt the moss off), never in the hearth room or on the stairs. per_m patches to a metre of damp wall, spacing_m apart, at most max, radius_m across. Drawn in the stone's own shader, with no light node, so nothing the game's rules read (the torch's light, the fires, the dark) knows it is there: the moss's own texels glow in color at energy, thickest at a patch's heart and ragged at its rim, and a faint light falls on the stone and floor within light_m of it, light_strength times as strong on them as its own texels' glow (tuned by eye in the walkabout: 4 picks out the stones round a patch in faint teal; 1 can't be seen; 10 is a lamp). Any flame (the torch in hand, a planted torch, the hearth, a relit holder or sconce) within dims_near_flame_m whose light reaches it (no stone between) fades it to dim_to of its rest over dims_s; once the flame has gone it creeps back to rest over returns_s. wall_life (WallLife): count beetles and scarabs a tomb (scarab_share of them scarabs) on its walls, more where it's damp and away from the fires, size_m long by kind, crawling at crawl_mps (by kind) for crawl_s, resting rest_s, height_m up the wall. When a flame's light falls on one within scatter_from_light_m it scuttles at flee_mps (faster if it must) to the nearest joint of the stone it is on (the wall's real joints) and squeezes in over sink_s, gone from view within gone_within_s; it waits hide_s, then comes out of its crack again over emerge_s once no flame's light is on it. colors: shell and legs, by kind. daylight_follows_clock: the crawler runs the world's clock (the 144-minute day; World turns it only once a planet is generated), and a shaft's daylight follows the sun's height over the tomb (smoke.json vents.daylight sky_band_deg, low_sun_share). puzzles false: none of it is ever needed to go on, and none of it marks a way. [NOT WIRED YET — design §FG, §EW.7] window_views (a stair up to a window over the wilderness, with the surface ruins) and vines_sway_on_pass (with a jungle style).
_help.folk_3d: The folk at the hearth are real 3D models of the shared rig, painted per §ES and made pixel by the 480-line frame and their texels (Mike: 'more like the goat pixel guy', frame 3), not baked billboards. Amends §ET.8 for folk; creatures and bosses stay sprites until Mike says (§FI.2 call 11). Built 7 Oct (Claude Code): the rescuer (who: hearth_folk; HearthFolk) is the shared rig in the scene, CloakedFigure with its beast head and cloak colours as before, seated on a low stone facing the hearth (rescuer). Painted per §ES: diffuse only, roughness 1, no normal maps, its occlusion baked toward navy (Prelit), lit live by the hearth's amber, casting the fire's shadow, its head's too. texels_per_m: its painted detail one value a texel on a grid of this many texels a metre in each part's own space (16: the tomb walls' fitted-stone grid, so it pixelates like them at 480 lines); its head on its own copy of the head's material, so no other head changes; 0 puts back the rig's fine weave and soft grain. step_fps: 0 runs its idle smooth at the frame rate (Claude Code's call: real geometry already moves a whole pixel at a time at 480 lines, and stepped head turns read as jerky); 8 steps it as the sprites stepped (sprites.anim_fps). render, painted, target: what it is, for the record.
_help.opening_pick: [NOT WIRED YET — design §FJ.1] Mike, 6 Oct 22:52: 'first tomb should be randomly selected from the entire roster'. A new game's first dungeon is any built ruin kind (a key of themes), picked at random from the new game's seed; opening.first_theme stays the fallback until this is wired. Amends §ET.3. Each new kind joins the draw as it's built.
_help.themes_aztec_temple: (Claude Code, queue 80, design §FN.1) themes.aztec_temple: the Aztec temple, built by the tomb's generator in masonry.json's aztec_temple stone with its two fixed chambers (room_pool.json always). It is drawn only when aztec_temple.json enabled is true (§FJ.1's roster, opening_pick); with it false (the default) no game ever draws it and the first ruin is the tomb as before. Which biome world it sits in is Mike's open call (§FN.8 call 1).
_help.calendar: (26 Oct; 29 Oct §GK.1.2) One calendar (date, season, clock hour and day length) for the hub and every realm (§FK.3). No latitude anywhere (§GK.1.2, superseding §GE.5.2-3): every sky, daylight and season value is read at reference_deg (35, never shown as a latitude), so a summer day is ~74/18/34/18 real minutes, an equinox ~60/18/48/18, a winter day ~51/18/57/18 everywhere; hub_latitude_deg and area_latitude_deg are no longer read (kept, superseded). winter_by_biome: what winter does on each kind of surface (snow and frost only where cold; §GE.5.4, which §GK.1.2 keeps). Year, tilt and phases stay in data/sky/day_cycle.json and data/seasons.json. start_year_day 0 = the spring equinox. Underground nothing seasonal changes; the shaft daylight follows the one shared sky (§FG, Vents.sun_deg). Wired 26 Oct (queue 114, CrawlerCalendar), to §GK.1.2 on 29 Oct: hub_area is the kind whose winter the hub has (tropical: a dry season, the plants keep their leaves); area_of_world maps a surface's world (worlds.json) to its kind where the names differ. A new game starts at start_year_day at dusk; Continue keeps the saved clock.

persistence.log_continue: Back by the hearth, as you left it.

stand_in.log: Up the old stair and out. Another tomb, another hearth.

cleared.log_line: Banished the dark. What lived in it fled.

light_field.of: the hearth, relit holders, planted torches

folk_3d.target: ozavry_ frame 3 (goat with bowl in rain)

hub._help: (design §GC.1-2, §FZ.1, queue 112; Mike 26 Oct: 'spawn in around the campfire at dusk and also set up a RNG camp sites for each of our specialized village niches') The hub camp on the surface (HubCamp, built on Surface's machinery): a bounded clearing closed in by cliffs and fog, its ground, kind and keepers' sites drawn from the game's seed and kept for the game (§FK). You start every session at its campfire at dusk; the way down is the old stair behind the fire, ringed with standing stones, into the dungeon; the dungeon's way out brings you back up into the camp. on false: the old start (waking by the hearth below) and the old surface over the ruin.
hub._help_across: How wide the clearing is (m), drawn from the seed in this range; the cliffs close it.
hub._help_dusk: dusk_into_min: how far into dusk (real minutes) every new game starts. Dusk begins at sunset on the crawler's clock (design §GE, CrawlerCalendar: the reference's stylised day, dusk the 18 minutes after the sun goes down). dusk_sun_deg is superseded by it (26 Oct, queue 114) and no longer read.
hub._help_biome: The camp's plants: data/biomes, by key, and which association grows in each zone (the river's banks, the clearing, under the cliffs).

surface._help: Laid over worlds.json surface for the hub only (same keys): taller crooked cliffs, the wash a river closer to the camp.

fire._help: The campfire: out_m in front of the stair's mouth (the way down opens just behind it); you spawn spawn_m from the fire on the far side, facing it.

kinds._help: The start kind, one per game from the seed: what towers round the clearing. Each lists its props: pillars (tall crooked rock stacks: how many, height m), roots (oversized arching roots), ruins (broken columns and fallen blocks), vines (hanging from the pillars).

ring._help: The standing stones round the way down (§GC.2: something stranger beneath the fire): how many, their height (m) and how far out from the stair's line.

shaman._help: The hooded cook-shaman (§FZ.1.6) at the cauldron beside the fire: cloak colours, how far from the fire, the cauldron's green glow (the frame's one green accent) and its light.
shaman._help_hang: (Mike, 26 Oct: 'the cauldron should be over the fire') The cauldron hangs from a tripod of poles straight over the campfire; hang_m the height of its middle over the fire's floor.
shaman._help_glow: glow_energy, glow_range_m: the brew's own light on what is round it. Faint on purpose: hung over the fire (26 Oct) its green added to the fire's amber washed the ground round the fire white and cyan at 1.4 over 5 m. The brew itself still glows (emissive) and blooms.
shaman._help_male: (design §GI.1, 27 Oct, Mike: 'historically the shamans have been men so itll be a male') The hub's shaman is a man: height_m, and a beard (beard colour) showing under the hood; the hood still hides his face. He keeps the pipe, the cauldron and the singing (§GH). The swamp witch of §FR is a different character, untouched.

keepers._help: The other five keepers' sites (§FZ.1; their looks and trades are still §FZ.4's to-do: the figures are plain hooded stand-ins in their trade's cloak colours). Each site is placed from the seed on a ring round the fire (within_m), apart_m from each other, clear of the stair and the river; the fisher-weaver's goes on the river bank. Props per keeper are built by HubCamp.

hunter_tanner.name: Hunter-tanner
hunter_tanner.props: drying rack with hides, a bone pile

fisher_weaver.name: Fisher-weaver
fisher_weaver.props: net frame, baskets, a fish line; on the river bank

knapper_potter.name: Knapper-potter
knapper_potter.props: clay kiln with a glowing mouth, pots, a flint pile

keepers._help_dress: (Mike, 26 Oct: 'more fleshed out ... consider the different niches') Each site also has a shelter in its trade's way and its trade's work round it, built by HubCamp._dress: hunter-tanner a hide tent, a hide on a hoop, a skull-and-antler totem, a spear rack, meat over a smoke pit; fisher-weaver a reed hut, a dugout on the bank, a fish-drying line, a fish trap, a basket; woodcutter-firekeeper a bark lean-to, a felled trunk with an axe in it, stumps, kindling bundles, the firekeeper's ember pot; forager-herbalist a thatched hut, a garden bed of strange flowers, gourds on a line, a mortar on a stone; knapper-potter a clay hut, the clay pit, pots drying on a plank, a knapping stone and flakes, the kiln's smoke. Every site has a torch post (torch_energy, torch_range_m) so it reads at dusk.

hub.log_start: Dusk at the camp. The fire crackles; the cauldron steams.
hub.log_down: Down the old steps beneath the fire, into the dark.
hub.log_up: Up out of the dark, into the camp.

common._help: The camp's common ground: log benches round the fire, a line of flat stepping stones from the fire to each keeper's site (step_m apart, stone_color; a solid worn-earth strip read as a black slab under the grade, 26 Oct), and totems (how many) about the clearing, one crowned with a skull and antlers.

hub._help_ground: ground_color: the camp's ground (forest floor, dark loam). It used the dungeon's world's desert sand before, which the glossy grade blew out to white round the fire (Mike, 26 Oct: 'the amount of light coming from the fire seems too bright').

cauldron_fx._help: (Mike, 26 Oct: 'lets get some effects steaming up off the cauldron- also, for different brews which would take different times there will be different effects') The camp cauldron's effects (CauldronFX). Each brew: brew_s how long it takes (0 = a pot that just simmers on); steam its colour and steam_rate how thick (0-1) at full boil; bubbles how hard it bubbles (0-1); sparks how many rising motes (0-1) and spark_kind what they are (embers, spores, motes, none); glow the brew's own colour (its surface and its faint light). Brewing, the steam, bubbles and motes build from a simmer to full over brew_s; done, a puff goes up and it holds at full for hold_s. Brews are first guesses tied to plants the design names (§FM.7, §FN, §FP, §FR); what each does is the brew system's to decide (not built). Until there is a way to ask for one, the cook-shaman works through cycle in order (rest_s of plain stew between).

camp_stew.name: Camp stew
camp_stew.note: the everyday pot: white steam, a slow bubble, the odd ember off the fire

healing_broth.name: Healing broth
healing_broth.note: herbs (the forager-herbalist's): pale green steam, a steady boil, a few green motes

ololiuhqui.name: Ololiuhqui (morning glory seed)
ololiuhqui.note: the Aztec world's vine (§FM.7, queue 72): violet steam curling, blue motes rising

teonanacatl.name: Teonanácatl (the flesh of the gods)
teonanacatl.note: the Aztec brew mushroom (§FN.5): thin magenta steam, slow thick bubbles, spores drifting up and wandering

blue_lotus.name: Blue lotus and mandrake
blue_lotus.note: Egypt's brew (§FP): blue mist, gold sparks

jimsonweed.name: Jimsonweed (datura)
jimsonweed.note: the swamp witch's (§FR): heavy sickly yellow-green smoke that rolls over the rim and sinks, a hard boil

cauldron_fx._help_spill: spill (0-1, 0 or absent none): a heavy brew's fog, billowing out over the rim and rolling down round the fire, spreading and fading on the ground (Mike, 26 Oct: 'a more billowing and flowing over the edges type of fog'). Jimsonweed spills hard; teonanácatl a little.

bank._help: (design §GJ.2) The bank at the hub, like PSO's: what is in it is never lost (death takes only what you carry, §GJ.1). Interact with it (reach_m) to open it: click a thing you carry to put it in, a thing in the bank to take it out; Esc or the interact button closes it. capacity: how many things it holds (a generous first guess). currency: the money's name (teeth, §FZ.3): a slot kept ready, since teeth are not built yet. Who or what keeps it is open (§GJ.2): for now a lidded store-basket beside the fire, opposite the shaman (from_fire_m). Kept in the game's save (§FK).
bank.log_open: You open the store by the fire.

areas._help: (design §GD.1.2-4, queue 113; §GH, queue 116) Realms (areas) reached from the hub by the shaman's song round the fire. Each realm is a curated, seeded surface with a main hearth near one edge, an overworld to explore and a ruin entrance (the old stair) down into its ruin; the ruin's way out brings you back up near the mouth. The interact button at the hub fire or beside the shaman (interact_reach_m) sits you down facing the fire; the shaman sings the song of a realm you know (songs), the flames take its colour and a glimpse of it opens in the fire (glimpse); left and right scroll through the realms you know; the interact button again steps you into the fire: the wash (travel.wash_s) and you come out at that realm's hearth. Moving or Esc stands you up with nothing changed. Knowing the song is the key (§GH.2.1); lighting a realm's hearth with your torch reclaims it (lit for good, saved, §FK) but no longer gates travel. Home: the interact button at the realm's hearth. on false: no travel.
areas._help_brand: brand: stepping through the fire with no lit torch, you carry a brand from the hub fire (a lit torch in hand): fire carried, never made (§ET), and the way to light the far hearth. Since 28 Oct (Mike: torches are found or made, never handed out; torch.json crawler_burn.supply.brand_without_torch false) the fire lights a torch you carry, and with none you go through with none.

travel._help: wash_s: the fire-wash in and out (seconds each way); flame_s how long the hub's flames hold the area's colour before you step through.

first._help: The first area: the surface over the game's first ruin (worlds.json surface, the ruin's own world), at areas size. across_m: how wide (a range, drawn from the seed; prompt's first guess 300-600). colour: the hub fire's flames when bound for it, and the wash. hearth: from_edge_m how far in from the cliff's foot the main hearth stands; reach_m how close your torch's flame must be; light_hold_s how long you hold it there.
first.name: The dry basin
first._help_realm: (§GK.2.4) realm: the song web's id for this area (song_web.json). The built first realm is the desert the cactus opens; its look as the Aztec dry highland scrub (§GK.1.4) is not built yet.

areas.log_link: The hearth catches. This place is reclaimed: its fire burns for good.
areas.log_home: The shaman's song carries you home through the fire.
areas.log_sing: You sit at the fire. The shaman begins to sing.
areas.log_step: You step into the fire as the song swells.
areas.log_stand: You get up from the fire.

songs._help: (§GH.1.2, §GH.2) Each realm's song, by realm key (areas.<key>). Knowing it is what puts the realm in the fire. known_from_start: the realms whose songs you know in a new game; a stand-in until Mike says how songs are learned (§GH.4 call 1, open; from tablets, tomes or the other peoples, §GG.1.3). Per song: music, a res:// path to Mike's track when it exists (used in place of the placeholder when the file is there); otherwise a placeholder generated from bpm (the drum), root_hz (the hummed chant's home note), chant (the tune, semitones from root, one per beat; null a rest) and drum (per beat: 1 a deep thump, 0.5 a light one, 0 none). The flames take the realm's colour (areas.<key>.colour) while it plays. Since §GK.2 (queue 116 amended): a new game knows no song (known_from_start applies only to saves from before §GK); songs are learned by giving the shaman a key plant (song_web.json).

glimpse._help: (§GH.1.3) The glimpse of the realm in the fire and smoke: a view from beside its hearth (from_hearth_m out, eye_m up, looking toward the realm's middle, drifting drift_deg round over drift_s), rendered px wide, shown size_m across hung height_m over the hub fire, toward_you_m out toward you; soft-edged and wavering with the heat (waver); it fades in over fade_s as the song begins.

sit._help: Where you sit: from_fire_m from the hub fire's middle on the side you came from, the view at eye_m, pitched to the fire.

death._help: (design §GI.2, §GJ.1, §GJ.3) Dying in a realm, on its surface or in its ruin: you wake at the hub fire with nothing carried (finds, gear, torches, the left hand's strip, currency). Everything you had drops where you fell as one pile (a bundle with a faint ember glow: glow_colour, glow_energy); it never despawns and is kept in the save per realm; walk to it (pickup_m) and it all comes back to you; dying again leaves another pile. What is in the bank (hub.bank) is untouched. What you carry is yours only once the shaman's song brings you home from the realm's hearth.
death.log_wake: Taken in the dark. You wake at the hub fire with nothing on you; all you carried lies where you fell.
death.log_pile: You gather up what you lost.
death._help_pages: (Mike, 27 Oct: 'tome pages should drop until you get it back to the hub') Tome pages you pick up are only carried until the shaman's song brings you home from a realm's hearth; die first and they drop in your pile with everything else, and lie nowhere else meanwhile (not back on their floor). Pages already brought home are never lost.

areas._help_standins: (§GK.2.4, queue 116 amended) Stand-in realms: songs you can learn (their key plants, song_web.json) whose places are not built yet. The shaman sings them and the flames take their colour, but no glimpse opens and stepping in is refused (log_standin). standin true marks one; remove it once its realm is built.
areas.log_standin: The song falters. The fire will not open there yet.

arrive._help: (§GK.3, queue 116 amended) Arriving: you hear the realm before you see it. After the wash the frame goes to near-dark (dark_colour at dark_alpha over to_dark_s) and holds sound_s with only the realm's own sounds; then its music (its song at music_db, fading in over music_in_s) for music_s more; then the picture settles (picture_s); the music eases off over music_fade_s. Claude Code's first guesses. on false: the old plain wash.
